newsitem.title: BERMUDA: NZ SPORT - Northern bowlers restrict England.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Northern bowlers restrict England.

text.p: HAMILTON, Jan 20 - Two of Northern Districts' unsung performers had a day to savour when they shared nine English wickets in their four-day cricket tour match here yesterday, NZPA reports.

Medium pacers Alex Tait and Scott Styris picked up five for 96 and four for 110 respectively as they restricted England to 294 in their first innings in reply to Northern Districts' poor first innings of 69.
At stumps last night Northern Districts had fared better in their second innings to be 99-1.
In a provincial side who have produced New Zealand test and one-day bowlers Simon Doull, Dion Nash, Richard de Groen and Roydon Hayes in recent seasons, Tait and Styris' chances have been limited.
However they reaped dividends yesterday by sticking to a good line on a pitch which offered some assistance.
"If you kept a good line and length, kept it reasonably full, the wicket did the rest and you gave yourself a good chance," Tait said last night.
He bowled 36.5 overs for his wickets, which represented his best first-class performance. In 10 first-class matches, Tait now has 30 wickets at an excellent average of 23.
Tait believed it was important Northern Districts bounced back from their first-day embarrassment.
"For both teams it is a practice game but it's always nice to do well against a touring team and we were a bit disappointed with the way we batted (in the first innings)."
Tait, who has spent the last five winters playing one-day cricket for Gore Court in Kent, is regarded as a one-day specialist but he'd like to make his mark in the four-day Shell Trophy.

He admitted he occasionally gets frustrated at not getting more first-class opportunities and it could be that he and Styris end up contesting one fast-medium place for the remainder of the Shell Trophy competition.
While Tait won the battle for the final wicket -- and better figures -- Styris impressed with his ability to beat the bat, and did remove three of the top six England batsmen.
"We thought we had nothing to lose and we had to show a bit of fight, and I thought we played quite well today," Styris said.
Styris, who has now taken 34 first-class wickets in nine matches, conquered one of his problems yesterday -- a tendency to over pitch.
"I have been guilty of throwing up a few half-volleys but I can only remember being driven once down the ground," he added.
Styris was a No 3 batsmen until the winter of 1994 when he went to Christchurch for a fast bowling clinic. That was before he made his first-class debut and the change became permanent.
He now has his sights set on a winter of playing league or club cricket in England.
Captain Blair Pocock and promising Matthew Bell rounded off a satisfying day for the home side by adding an unbroken 90 runs for the second wicket.
While Pocock's first-test opening partner Bryan Young was out cheaply for a second time in the match, Pocock had a good look at the England bowlers on his way to an unbeaten 60.
Bell battled his way to 35 by stumps as the pair gave England's bowlers their most stubborn resistance in the first-class matches on tour so far.
